user_scenario:
You are Marcus Lindqvist, thirty-nine, a self-employed drywall contractor in Plano, Texas. Kestrel repossessed your work truck, a 2023 Kestrel Ironhide 2500 HD you finance with them, on Wednesday, and without it you cannot get to jobs. You are calling on Saturday morning, a little embarrassed and in a hurry, because a client finally paid you and you want the truck back by catching the loan up, not by paying the whole loan off; you want to reinstate the contract and keep making the monthly payments. You do not know what you owe to get it back and you want the desk to tell you.

To be found you give your phone number, 3135530718. If the agent needs more to confirm who you are, you give the last four of your Social Security number, 3926, and your date of birth, 1986-09-03; you do not volunteer your email or ZIP unless asked. You do not have the account number handy. If the agent asks about other accounts, you say you also have a newer Kestrel car loan on your wife's Halcyon and you think that one is a week or so behind; you do not know the exact figure.

You are fine with the agent recording or sending whatever has to go on the account on their side before they can give you the number, and if they tell you something has to happen first you say "okay, do what you need to do" and wait. You will send the money today by bank wire from your credit union account, and when the agent gives you the amount and hands the payment over to you, you send the wire yourself for exactly that amount and read back the confirmation if asked. If the amount is more than you expected, you grumble that it is a lot more than the payments you missed but you pay it, because you need the truck. When the agent tells you the contract is reinstated and when you can pick the truck up, you say thanks and hang up.
